# RFI-023: Area B slab on grade: concrete strength, S-001 vs 03 30 00

**Conflict confirmed.** S-001 General Note 5 requires 3,500 psi at 28 days
for slabs on grade, and Detail 3/S-101 sends the slab strength back to that
note. Specification Section 03 30 00, paragraph 2.6.C, requires 4,000 psi at
28 days for slabs-on-grade with a maximum water-cementitious materials ratio
of 0.45. Submittal 03 30 00-02 was returned "No Exceptions Taken" by the
Structural Engineer with slab mix M-2 at 3,500 psi and a w/cm of 0.48, so
the mix in hand meets the drawing note and not the specification. The two
documents cannot both be satisfied by the returned mix.

## Question

Please confirm whether the Area B slab on grade is to be placed at 4,000
psi per Section 03 30 00, paragraph 2.6.C, with the contractor resubmitting
slab mix M-2 at 4,000 psi and a maximum w/cm of 0.45 for review, or whether
the 3,500 psi mix M-2 returned "No Exceptions Taken" on Submittal
03 30 00-02 may be placed as approved.

S-001 General Note 5 lists 3,500 psi for slabs on grade, and Detail 3/S-101
refers the slab strength to that note. Section 03 30 00, paragraph 2.6.C,
requires 4,000 psi, a maximum w/cm of 0.45, and 3 percent maximum air for
interior slabs to receive a hard-troweled finish. Because the returned submittal carries one of the two values, the
contractor is asking rather than placing at either strength.

## References

- S-001, General Note 5: minimum compressive strengths at 28 days, normal
  weight (145 pcf); "Slabs on grade: 3,500 psi"; footings and grade beams
  3,000 psi; foundation walls and piers 4,000 psi.
- S-001, General Note 9: design mixtures for each class of concrete to be
  submitted to the Structural Engineer for review before placement and to
  demonstrate the specified compressive strength.
- S-101, Plan keynote 4: Area B slab on grade, T.O. slab 100'-0", see
  3/S-101.
- S-101, Detail 3/S-101, Typical Slab-on-Grade Section: 5" slab on grade,
  6x6-W2.9xW2.9 welded wire reinforcement at mid-depth, 4" compacted
  aggregate base; detail note "Concrete strength per S-001 General Note 5."
- Section 03 30 00, Cast-in-Place Concrete, paragraph 1.4.B: design
  mixtures submitted for each concrete mixture, alternate design mixtures
  submitted when circumstances warrant adjustment, subject to review by the
  Structural Engineer before placement.
- Section 03 30 00, paragraph 2.6.C: "Slabs-on-Grade: Compressive strength
  4,000 psi at 28 days; maximum water-cementitious materials ratio 0.45;
  slump 4 inches, plus or minus 1 inch; air content 3 percent maximum for
  interior slabs to receive a hard-troweled finish."
- Section 03 30 00, paragraph 2.6.D: foundation walls and piers at 4,000
  psi, maximum w/cm 0.45, air content 5.5 percent plus or minus 1.5 percent
  (the approved 4,000 psi mix M-3 is air entrained to this paragraph and is
  not a hard-troweled slab mix).
- Submittal 03 30 00-02, Concrete Design Mixtures, returned September 21,
  2026 by Tremont Engineering Group, "No Exceptions Taken": mix M-2, slabs
  on grade, 3,500 psi, maximum w/cm 0.48, not air entrained, noted "Per
  S-001 Note 5"; reviewer stamp comment that review does not relieve the
  Contractor of responsibility for compliance with the Contract Documents.
- Referenced but not reviewed: Typical Detail 6/S-501 (construction joints,
  cited by S-101 keynote 7); Specification Section 07 26 00 (vapor
  retarder, cited by Detail 3/S-101).

## Suggested resolution

None proposed; request direction. A proposal would need the Structural
Engineer to state which of the two strength values was intended for the
Area B slab.

## Impact

- Cost: Potential. The concrete subcontractor's price is based on the
  3,500 psi mix M-2 returned on Submittal 03 30 00-02; the subcontractor
  reports the difference between the two mixes is small, but no figure has
  been provided and nothing has been priced.
- Schedule: Potential. The Area B slab-on-grade pour is scheduled for
  October 23, 2026, and Ridgeline Ready Mix needs three working days after
  the strength is confirmed to resubmit and batch a revised mix, so the pour
  cannot proceed until this RFI is answered.
- The requested response date of October 19, 2026 is 7 calendar days from
  issue, shorter than the 14-calendar-day contract turnaround under the
  Supplementary Conditions (October 26, 2026), because the turnaround date
  falls after the pour. If the answer becomes a change, the project manager
  should check the contract's notice provisions; this RFI is not a notice
  and not legal advice.
